h1: The 8 Best 8-Quart Air Fryers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 large air fryers from 8 to 10 quarts, compared on basket layout, controls and cooking modes, from Ninja DualZone to Chefman.
summary: The Ninja DZ201 Foodi DualZone is the best 8 quart air fryer: two independent baskets with Match Cook and Smart Finish for $100 to $200. The DZ401 adds 10 quarts for big families, and the DZ550 adds a cook thermometer. The Chefman and Gourmia single-basket models are the budget options.
intro: Eight quarts is where an air fryer stops being a snack gadget and starts replacing a weeknight oven. The catch is that quarts alone say little. One huge basket and two medium baskets cook very differently, and the second layout is the one that saves dinner, because a main and a side can finish together instead of one going cold while the other cooks.

We reviewed eight current models on paper, from a single-basket 8 Qt to dual-basket 10 Qt Ninjas. Several run above 8 quarts, which we kept because they are the real alternatives at this size. Ranking starts with basket layout, then controls, cooking modes and cleanup, using spec sheets and owner reports, not cooking trials, so confirm basket dimensions and wattage on the live listing.

products.name: Ninja DZ201 Foodi 8 Quart 6-in-1 DualZone 2-Basket Air Fryer
products.verdict: Two 8-quart-total baskets with Match Cook and Smart Finish. The default choice.
products.description:
The DZ201 is an 8 quart six-in-one with two independent baskets. Its listing highlights Match Cook and Smart Finish, which sync two different foods to finish at the same time, plus modes such as roast, broil and dehydrate. It sells for $100 to $200. Two zones are the biggest practical upgrade in this category: chicken in one, potatoes in the other, both done together.

It wins because dual baskets turn an air fryer from a side-dish tool into a dinner appliance. The single-basket Chefman picks cost less but cannot sync two foods. Against the DZ401, it stays smaller and cheaper.

Buy it for family dinners. The caveat is that each basket is smaller than a single 8 Qt basket, so one large item such as a whole chicken will not fit. Skip it if you cook one big item at a time.
products.idealFor: Families cooking a main and a side together.
products.skipIf: You cook one large item at a time.

products.name: Ninja DZ401 Foodi 10 Quart 6-in-1 DualZone XL 2-Basket Air Fryer
products.verdict: A 10 quart DualZone XL with two baskets for family-sized meals.
products.description:
The DZ401 is a 10 quart DualZone XL with two baskets and six cooking modes, including roast, broil and dehydrate. It keeps the Match Cook and Smart Finish features of its smaller sibling and sells for $100 to $200. The extra two quarts matter for a household of five or six, where an 8 quart split in two can feel small.

It ranks just behind the DZ201 because most buyers do not need the extra capacity, and the larger body takes more counter. The extra volume is real, though, and it beats every single-basket pick here for feeding six people. Against the DoubleStack, it spreads side by side instead of stacking.

Buy it if you regularly cook for a crowd. The caveat is size: measure your counter and the cabinet above it first. Skip it if counter space is tight.

products.name: Ninja DZ550 Foodi 10 Quart 6-in-1 DualZone Smart XL Air Fryer
products.verdict: A DualZone XL with a built-in cook thermometer for accurate doneness.
products.description:
The DZ550 adds an integrated Foodi Smart Thermometer to the 10 quart DualZone XL design, and sells for $100 to $200. The probe reads the internal temperature of meat so you cook to doneness instead of guessing by time. That matters for chicken and pork, where the difference between juicy and dry is a few degrees and a few minutes.

It ranks third because the thermometer is the only real step up over the DZ401, and not everyone cooks meat that way. It beats both Chefman models on features, but sits above them in cost. If you mostly cook frozen foods, the probe is wasted.

Best for roasting chicken, pork and steak. The caveat is the same size and counter footprint as the other 10 quart Ninjas, and a higher price than the DZ401. Skip it if you mostly cook frozen foods.
products.idealFor: Anyone roasting meat who wants accurate doneness.

products.name: Ninja Foodi Air Fryer (DZ550GY, 10 Qt DualZone Smart XL)
products.verdict: The same 10 Qt DualZone Smart XL with thermometer, listed under model DZ550GY.
products.description:
This listing is the 10 quart DualZone Smart XL with the integrated Foodi Smart Thermometer, sold as model DZ550GY. It has the same two independent baskets, Match Cook and Smart Finish modes as its sibling, and sells for $200 to $500. Treat it as the same machine under a different model code and finish.

It ranks fourth, just below the DZ550, because it duplicates that machine's features rather than adding any. Price and availability decide between the two, and the cheaper listing at the time of purchase should win. Note that this listing sits in a higher price bucket than the DZ550, which is a reason to compare before you buy.

Best for buyers who prefer this colorway or find it in stock. The caveat is that it offers nothing the DZ550 does not. Skip it if you already compared the DZ550 and prefer it.
pros: DualZone Smart Finish and Match Cook
products.idealFor: Buyers who find this listing cheaper than the DZ550.
products.skipIf: You already compared the DZ550 and prefer it.

products.name: Ninja Air Fryer DoubleStack XL (SL401)
products.verdict: Stacks two baskets vertically for roughly half the counter width.
products.description:
The DoubleStack XL, model SL401, is a 10 quart six-in-one that stacks its baskets vertically. Two removable meal racks per basket let you cook up to four foods at once. It sells for $200 to $500. Stacking saves counter width, which suits narrow kitchens where a side-by-side body would stick out over the edge.

It ranks fifth because the stacked design needs vertical clearance, and the baskets are less roomy than the side-by-side Ninjas. For a small counter, it beats every wide model above it, but the DZ201 gives roomier baskets for less money. Against the Chefmans, it brings dual-basket cooking at a higher cost.

Best for compact kitchens that still want dual-basket cooking. The caveat is height, so check that it fits under your cabinets. Skip it if your cabinets sit low over the counter.
products.idealFor: Small kitchens that want dual baskets.
products.skipIf: Your cabinets sit low over the counter.

products.name: Chefman Air Fryer 8 Qt
products.verdict: A straightforward single-basket 8 Qt with a nonstick, dishwasher-safe basket.
products.description:
Chefman gives you a single 8 quart basket with bake, dehydrate and frozen-food settings, and an XL nonstick basket that is dishwasher safe. A 450 degree finishing crisp setting is there for the last minutes of cooking. It sells for $50 to $100. A single large basket suits a batch of fries or a large cut that two smaller baskets would crowd.

It ranks sixth because simplicity is its strength and its limit: one basket means one food at a time. It undercuts the Ninjas on price, which is why it beats the Crispinator on value. Compared with the Gourmia, it has fewer presets but the dishwasher-safe basket.

Best for a budget-minded kitchen that wants one big basket. The caveat is that you cannot sync two foods like on a DualZone. Skip it if you cook a main and a side together.
products.idealFor: Budget kitchens that want one big basket.
products.skipIf: You cook a main and a side together.

products.name: Chefman Crispinator Air Fryer 6-in-1 with 8 Qt capacity
products.verdict: A viewing window and dial controls on an 8 Qt single basket.
products.description:
The Crispinator is a six-in-one 8 quart single-basket fryer with dial controls, a viewing window and a nonstick ceramic basket. A DC motor reaches 450 degrees for steady convection. It sells for $50 to $100. Dials set time and temperature directly, which is quicker than a touchscreen menu, and the window shows browning without releasing heat.

It ranks seventh because the window and dials are conveniences, not cooking upgrades, and it competes with the plainer Chefman above. Compared with the Gourmia, it offers fewer preset programs but more direct control. Against the Ninjas, it cannot sync two foods.

Best for people who dislike touchscreens and want to watch food crisp. The caveat is that it is still a single basket with fewer presets. Skip it if you want preset menus.
products.idealFor: Cooks who prefer dials to touchscreens.

products.name: Gourmia Air Fryer - 8 Qt Extra Large Capacity
products.verdict: A digital display with 12 presets and FryForce 360 for single-basket cooking.
products.description:
Gourmia offers an 8 quart basket with a digital display, twelve one-touch presets and FryForce 360 airflow technology. It also covers roast and bake modes and sells for $50 to $100. Presets suit beginners because they set time and temperature for common foods, which removes the guesswork on a first cook.

It ranks last because presets help beginners but do not change the fundamental single-basket limit, and the Chefman models sit in a similar tier. It has the widest preset library of the single-basket units. Against the Ninja DZ201, it cannot cook two foods in sync.

Best for beginners who want one-touch cooking. The caveat is that preset timing may need tweaks for your food. Skip it if you want dual baskets.

whatMatters.detail: A dual-basket fryer lets two foods cook at different settings and finish together. A single big basket suits one large item or a big batch of fries. Decide whether you cook a main and a side at once. If so, choose a dual-basket model like the Ninja DZ201, which finishes both together. Dual baskets also let you cook fish and vegetables without mixing flavors.

Dual-basket quarts are split between two baskets, so an 8 quart dual is two smaller baskets, not one big one. Compare the capacity of a single basket, not the total on the box, against what you cook. A 4 quart half crowds a large cut, which a single 8 quart basket handles more easily.

Large air fryers are tall, and some stacked designs need extra clearance. Measure the space under your cabinets and add room for the exhaust vent at the back. The Ninja DoubleStack saves width but needs height, so check both before you buy a larger model, and leave space behind it for hot exhaust air.

Nonstick and ceramic coatings clean easily, but they scratch if you use metal utensils. A dishwasher-safe basket, like the Chefman 8 Qt lists, saves effort. Check the listing before buying, and plan on hand-washing coated baskets with soft tools to extend their life. Scratched coating flakes and ruins the basket.

whatMatters.factor: Decide if you want a probe
whatMatters.detail: An integrated thermometer, as on the Ninja DZ550, lets you cook meat to a temperature rather than a timer. If you roast often, it is worth paying for, because it removes the guesswork about doneness. If you mostly cook frozen foods, skip the premium, and spend the difference on a second basket or accessories.

faq.q: Is a dual-basket air fryer worth it?
faq.a: For a main plus a side, yes. Match Cook on the Ninja DZ201 finishes two different foods at the same time. For one big batch, a single basket such as the Chefman 8 Qt is simpler and cheaper.

faq.q: What is the difference between the DZ550 and the DZ550GY?
faq.a: The two listings describe the same 10 quart DualZone Smart XL with an integrated thermometer. The DZ550GY is a different model code, so buy whichever is cheaper at the time, since the listing is the only real difference.

faq.q: Will a 10 quart model fit my counter?
faq.a: Large Ninjas need plenty of counter. The DoubleStack XL stacks vertically to save width, but check height under cabinets. The DZ401 and DZ550 are 10 quart and take real room, and the exhaust needs space behind them.

Yes. The Chefman 8 Qt has a frozen setting, and frozen foods often cook fast, and the Ninja models cover roast, broil and dehydrate modes for other tasks. Shake or flip the food halfway for even browning.

faq.q: How do I clean the basket?
faq.a: The Chefman 8 Qt lists a dishwasher-safe nonstick basket, while other models use nonstick coatings that are best hand-washed with soft tools. Avoid metal utensils on the Crispinator's ceramic basket too, and let baskets cool before washing.

It is a Ninja DualZone feature that copies settings from one basket to the other so both cook the same way. Smart Finish times two baskets so they end together, which suits a main and a side that need different times.

finalTake: Buy the Ninja DZ201 for most households, since two baskets that finish together beat one large one. Move to the DZ401 for five or six people and the DZ550 if you roast meat. Take the DoubleStack when counter width is tight, and a Chefman or Gourmia only if a single basket and a lower price suit your cooking.
